title: Crystal Palace set to complete £7.5m deal for Ajax defender Jaïro Riedewald
trail: The Dutch defender Jaïro Riedewald is set to be reunited with his former manager at Ajax, Frank de Boer, after reaching an agreement in principle to move to Crystal Palace
body: The Holland defender Jaïro Riedewald is set to be reunited with his former manager at Ajax, Frank de Boer, after reaching an agreement in principle to move to Crystal Palace. The versatile defender, who can also operate as a holding midfielder, is expected to cost about £7.5m with further add-ons related to appearances and achievements. Reports in the Netherlands suggest the Ajax director of football, Marc Overmars, has sanctioned the sale unless further interest emerges from rival suitors. West Bromwich Albion, Leicester City, Everton and Stoke City had all considered moves for the 20-year-old, who has three caps. Riedewald, who was given his first-team debut by De Boer in 2013, will add to Palace’s defensive options, with the club having accepted they will not be able to bring Mamadou Sakho back to Selhurst Park, because of Liverpool’s £30m asking price. Scott Dann, who began last season as Palace’s captain, will remain at the club and Chelsea’s Ruben Loftus-Cheek completed a one-year loan move on Wednesday. The England under-21 international told the club’s website: “I had the option of coming to Palace and I thought that it would be great for me. I live not too far away, I was born in Lewisham and Palace is good club so I thought it’s a good chance to play here and be a part of the team. They have a very strong team and I’d like to be a part of that this season.” There is interest, too, in Barcelona’s reserve goalkeeper, Jasper Cillessen, who could join on loan for the season with a view to a permanent transfer. Palace sold Steve Mandanda back to Marseille on Tuesday after only one year, with the France No2 goalkeeper signing a three-year contract at the Stade Vélodrome. Sakho set to be left out of Liverpool tour Mamadou Sakho does not expect to be included in Liverpool’s squad for their tour to Hong Kong, with his future some distance from being resolved and potential suitors put off by the £30m asking price. Crystal Palace had explored the possibility of bringing the France international back to Selhurst Park, where he enjoyed an impressive loan spell over the second half of last season, but would be reluctant to meet Liverpool’s valuation. Sakho’s former club, Paris Saint-Germain, are seeking to add a fourth central defender to their squad and could turn back to a player who graduated through their youth ranks and captained the first team at the age of 17. The French club, whose recruitment is being overseen by the new sporting director, Antero Henrique, have expressed an interest in Manchester City’s Eliaquim Mangala, who has also been courted by Lyon. Yet their preference would be to take the 26-year-old initially on loan rather than meet City’s £20m asking price, aware that Valencia, for whom Mangala played 30 La Liga games last season, opted against making his move permanent. There has been no contact from PSG regarding Sakho, who retains iconic status with the club’s supporters, but a return to Parc des Princes may appeal to the 27-year-old. He would potentially compete with the captain Thiago Silva, Marquinhos and the youth academy graduate Presnel Kimpembe for first-team opportunities. The French club confirmed the arrival of Dani Alves on a two-year deal on Wednesday following his release from Juventus. Sakho has not represented Liverpool since April 2016 and spent the first half of last season playing for the under-23s before proving his pedigree at Palace. Sam Allardyce’s team won five of the seven games he completed, keeping four clean sheets, including in a 3-0 win over Arsenal, with the Frenchman’s contribution seen as a key part of the side’s recovery to finish 14th. Liverpool, who will be without Sadio Mané in Hong Kong as the Senegalese continues his rehabilitation from a knee injury, are confident they will be able to secure an acceptable fee for Sakho and point to Everton’s willingness to pay a similar amount for Michael Keane as evidence of the going rate for experienced Premier League defenders. Sakho has two years still on his contract and has been working at Melwood on his fitness over the summer. He is not involved in Liverpool’s friendly against Tranmere Rovers on Wednesday night and would not expect to take part in Friday’s fixture against Wigan. Jürgen Klopp’s team depart for east Asia on Sunday, where they will play Palace in the Premier League Trophy. Zouma poised to join Stoke on loan Kurt Zouma is to sign a new four-year contract at Chelsea before joining the exodus of young players seeking regular first-team football on loan from Stamford Bridge, with Stoke City expected to secure the French defender for the season. A number of clubs have expressed an interest in the 22-year-old centre-half, who returned last term after a nine-month absence with knee ligament damage, and West Bromwich Albion had hoped to lure him to the Hawthorns. Yet Stoke are likeliest to secure Zouma having agreed a deal in principal which would include covering his wages for the campaign ahead, with the youngster permitted to miss training at Cobham on Wednesday to finalise the move. Zouma will join Ruben Loftus-Cheek (Crystal Palace), Kasey Palmer (Huddersfield Town) and Tammy Abraham (Swansea City) in sealing a temporary switch to a rival topflight club, with Izzy Brown expected to join them by joining newly promoted Brighton & Hove Albion. West Ham fail with £20m Arnautovic bid Stoke have rejected a £20m bid from West Ham for Marko Arnautovic. The 28-year-old forward handed in a transfer request this week but Stoke have a strong bargaining position with Arnautovic only 12 months into a four-year contract. He is with the squad in Switzerland for their pre-season training camp. PA
